title: DMT Code chronology
description: Schema for public/timeline.json. Every entry is a dated record of published research, a legal decision, a platform fact, or a community claim. The evidence_class field states which of those it is, and nothing is presented as research unless its identifier resolves to the work described. To add a paper or article, append one object to entries that validates against #/definitions/entry.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file was authored against.

provenance.description: How the citations in this file were checked, and when.

verified_on.description: ISO date of the most recent full citation verification pass.

verified_against.description: Which authorities the citations were resolved against.

rule.description: The standing rule the file is maintained under.

evidence_classes.description: Human-readable definition of each evidence_class value. Every value used by an entry must have a key here.

entries.description: The chronology. Order in the file is not significant; sort on date.sort_key.

entry.description: One dated record. Omit any optional key you cannot fill truthfully. Never set a key to null, an empty string, or a placeholder such as Unknown, TBD, or n/a.

id.description: Stable url-safe slug. Used as the drill-in route at /timeline/{id}. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only. Must be unique across the file and must never be changed once published, because links depend on it. Convention: firstauthor-year-shortsubject.

headline.description: Short title for the entry. Plain sentence case. No HTML.

summary.description: What the work found or what happened, in plain language, and where relevant what it does not establish. No HTML. State only what the cited source supports.

people.description: People the entry is about, for the sort-by-person view. Include only named individuals actually identified by the source.

tags.description: Lowercase hyphenated topic tags for filtering. Reuse existing tags rather than coining near-duplicates.

evidence_class.description: What kind of thing this is. Determines how the UI presents it. Anything without a resolvable published identifier belongs in community_report and is not shown as evidence.

date.description: When it happened, to whatever precision is actually known. Do not guess a month or day to make a date look complete.

precision.description: Which fields are real. year means month and day are unknown and must be omitted. month means day is unknown and must be omitted.

sort_key.description: Zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD used for sorting only. Unknown month or day is written as 00, which sorts before January without implying it. When two year-only entries share a year, increment the day segment (1994-00-00, 1994-00-01) to fix their relative order. Never render this to a user.

name.description: Display name as the source spells it, diacritics included.

sort.description: Surname in plain ASCII, for a sort that does not break on diacritics. Szara for Szara, Kluver for Kluver.

place.description: Where the work was done. Omit the whole object unless the source states it. Do not infer a city from an author's later affiliation.

source.description: The citation. Fill only fields the source actually supports. An identifier goes in here only after it has been resolved and the returned title read back and matched. Never write a DOI, ISBN or URL you have not resolved.

authors.description: Authors as printed, in printed order.

container.description: Journal, publication or venue the work appeared in.

doi.description: Bare DOI, no https://doi.org prefix. Must resolve at api.crossref.org/works/{doi} to the work named in title.

citation.description: Formal citation string where no DOI or ISBN applies, such as a law report reference.

note.description: Required for community_report. States plainly that no published source exists and that the entry is recorded as history, not offered as evidence.
